description: Defines RuntimeError_ with line tracking, Closure dataclass (param, body, env) for first-class functions, and Environment class implementing lexical scoping via linked list. Environment supports lookup (walks parent chain), bind (mutates current frame), and extend (creates child frame). Foundation for evaluator.

steps.description: Imports and RuntimeError_ exception: stores message with optional line prefix for error reporting.
Closure dataclass: captures param (str), body (AST node), env (Environment) at definition site. This is how functions carry their lexical scope. __repr__ shows param name.
Environment.__init__: bindings dict for this frame, parent reference for enclosing scope. Empty parent = global scope.
lookup: checks current bindings, then recurses to parent. If not found anywhere, raises RuntimeError_ with variable name and line.
bind: mutates current frame's bindings dict, returns self for chaining.
extend: creates new Environment with self as parent, binds name to value in child, returns child. Used for let and function call frames.

Linked-list environment: lookup walks parent chain (lexical scoping). extend creates new frame without mutating parent (immutable extension). bind mutates in place (for letrec/updates). Three operations, three purposes.

steps.answer: The Closure captures the Environment at the point of the Fun expression (which includes the let binding). When called, the evaluator creates a new child environment from that captured env, binds the parameter, and evaluates the body. The let variable remains accessible.
steps.question: When a Closure is created inside a let binding, what environment does it capture, and what happens when that closure is later called?

steps.description: Output: Value types and Environment defined.

title: Values and Environments: Closure and Linked-List Environment
